title: K-th highest bid
prompt:
An auction has received bids, and k winners will each pay the lowest winning bid. Return the k-th highest value in bids. Equal bids count separately, so in [5, 5, 3] the 2nd highest is 5.

- bids has 1 to 100,000 integers between -10^6 and 10^6.
- 1 <= k <= len(bids).
- Target O(n) average time. Sorting everything works but is O(n log n).
hints: The k-th highest of n values is the value that would sit at index n − k in ascending order.
Partition around a pivot. If the pivot lands at n − k you are done; otherwise keep only the side that contains that index.
Pick the middle element as pivot so sorted input does not degrade to O(n²). A random pivot works too.

solution.explanation: Quickselect looks for the value that belongs at index n − k after sorting. Each round swaps the middle element to the end as the pivot, moves smaller values to its left and places it at store, its final sorted position. If store is the target the pivot is the answer; otherwise the search narrows to the side that holds the target. A copy keeps the caller's list unchanged.

complexity.notes: The window roughly halves each round, so work is about 2n. Unlucky pivots give O(n²) in the worst case. A size-k min-heap is O(n log k) with O(k) space and works on streams.

followUps: Solve it with a size-k min-heap. When is that better than quickselect?
Bids keep arriving. Report the k-th highest after each one.
